title: WezTerm only uses a quarter of its window under native Wayland
body: I am using Arch Linux with hyprland-git and WezTerm 20250730-195751-6a493f88 under native Wayland. When WezTerm starts maximized, its terminal content only uses about a quarter of the window instead of the full area. The log says it cannot resize to the requested rows and columns because the window state is maximized. Disabling native Wayland with config.enable_wayland = false avoids the issue, but I would prefer native Wayland. Floating or resizing the window, setting initial_rows and initial_cols, and reinstalling both WezTerm and Hyprland did not fix it.

symptoms_visible: When WezTerm opens under native Wayland, the window is maximized but the terminal content occupies only about one quarter of it.
With native Wayland disabled, the terminal fills the window, although its rendering looks pixelated.
Floating the window, resizing it, changing initial rows or columns, and reinstalling WezTerm and Hyprland have not changed the quarter-sized content.
N0.label: N0 quarter-sized Wayland surface reported

symptoms_visible: With adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size set to false, the terminal content still occupies only a quarter of the native Wayland window.
N1_x.label: N1_x font-size window adjustment aftermath

symptoms_visible: The terminal continues to use roughly one quarter of the surface while the window is floated, maximized, or manually resized.
Other affected Hyprland systems using non-default monitor scale values show the same quarter-window rendering.
N2.label: N2 resizing behavior and monitor-scale reproduction collected

symptoms_visible: On the affected native Wayland setups with non-default monitor scale values, WezTerm still renders its terminal in only part of the available window.
N3.label: N3 Hyprland regression range supplied

symptoms_visible: On another affected user's current native Wayland setup, WezTerm now fills the window and the quarter-sized rendering cannot be reproduced even with a non-default monitor scale value.
I no longer have my original Arch, Hyprland, and WezTerm setup, so I cannot personally retest the original problem.
N_terminal.label: terminal closed after external non-reproduction without reporter retest

solution.intent: Disable automatic window resizing when the font size changes.

edges.comment: Real thread c0-c3, reporter's system: participant1 suggested disabling adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size; the reporter added it to the configuration and reported that the quarter-sized content remained.

question_patterns: What happens when the window opens floating, and does manually resizing or maximizing it change the content area?
Can you resize the floating window by its edges and describe how the terminal content responds?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It opens as a normal floating window, but the terminal content still takes only a quarter of it. Toggling maximize with Alt+Enter and manually resizing the edges do not change that; the content remains confined to a quarter at every window size.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The content immediately expands to fill the surface as soon as I manually resize the window.
The same quarter-sized area remains, but I used a mouse binding rather than Alt+Enter to resize and maximize it.

question_patterns: Can you run WezTerm with resize tracing enabled, resize or maximize the window, and share the raw logs and a recording?
Please capture WEZTERM_LOG=wezterm_gui::termwindow::resize=trace output while reproducing the behavior.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran it with the requested WEZTERM_LOG setting, resized and maximized the window, and uploaded the resulting wezterm_logs.txt file and a screen recording of the behavior.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The trace shows that WezTerm receives the new dimensions and the terminal fills the full surface throughout the recording.

question_patterns: Can anyone else reproduce this on Hyprland, and what monitor scale value is configured?
Does this also occur on another native Wayland system where the monitor scale value is not 1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it with upstream Hyprland and upstream WezTerm on a 3840x2160 monitor configured at scale 2. Foot fills its half of the screen, while WezTerm uses only one quarter of its window, and I see the same maximized resize warning.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can only reproduce it at scale 1, while scale 2 works correctly.
I reproduce the same quarter-window behavior at scale 1.5 rather than scale 2.

question_patterns: Did the behavior begin after a Hyprland update?
Which Hyprland versions were working and affected on another reproducible system?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my affected system it appeared after upgrading Hyprland from 0.50.1 to 0.51.0; WezTerm now shows the same incorrectly sized content.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The problem began after a WezTerm update while Hyprland stayed on 0.50.1, and reverting WezTerm alone removes it.

edges.comment: Real thread c4-c12. The float/maximize behavior and trace upload are from the original reporter in c5 and c9. Reproduction details from the affected Hyprland users in c7 and c10-c12 are folded into the simulated user side; their setups are not represented as changes to the reporter's machine.

question_patterns: Can you bisect Hyprland between the last working and first affected versions and share the resulting commit or range?
Please test Hyprland revisions between the working release and 0.51 and paste the raw bisection result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I bisected Hyprland and ended at https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/commit/00da4450db9bab1abfda169eefec8dab98f63a0b. I also opened https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/discussions/11727#discussioncomment-14429037 with the result.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Hyprland bisection does not produce a transition: the same WezTerm build is affected across all revisions back through the last supposedly working release.
I obtained the same final commit URL using a narrower set of Hyprland revisions.

edges.comment: Real thread c20-c22, participant13's Hyprland system folded into the user side. The answer preserves only the raw bisection endpoint and discussion URL. Interpreting that revision as the trigger for a WezTerm fractional-scaling defect is engineer-side inference on the final solution edge.

solution.intent: Use a current WezTerm nightly or git build containing the merged native-Wayland scaling fix, remove any temporary forced-DPI override, fully terminate old WezTerm processes, and verify the original quarter-window behavior on the affected scaled display.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a current nightly/git build after the merged fix. If a doubled or quadrupled config.dpi workaround was added, remove it, fully kill the existing WezTerm process, restart under native Wayland, and check whether the terminal now fills the window.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied only the raw Hyprland bisection endpoint. Maintainers connected the behavior to WezTerm's known native-Wayland fractional-scaling problems and later reported that a fix had merged. The thread does not describe the patch's internal mechanism, so the diagnosis must remain at that level.

edges.comment: Resolution chain from c21-c33. A maintainer requested testing a current nightly after a fix merged. Later DPI complaints were a separate post-fix configuration issue caused by retaining a manual DPI workaround and not fully restarting. In c32, participant18 reported that the original quarter-window symptom was no longer reproducible under fractional scaling. The original reporter stated in c33 that they had moved to Void, Niri, and Foot and therefore could not retest; closure was based on the other affected user's evidence, not reporter verification.

solution.intent: Use a current WezTerm nightly or git build containing the merged native-Wayland scaling fix, clean up any forced-DPI workaround, fully restart WezTerm, and verify that its terminal fills the window.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a current nightly/git build after the merged fix, remove any temporary manual config.dpi multiplier, fully terminate WezTerm, and retest under native Wayland.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the eventual current-build fix immediately. It skips the failed font-size adjustment, cross-system reproduction, resize traces, and Hyprland bisection that established the native-Wayland scaling diagnosis.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the first real suggestion was a falsified configuration change. It allows an agent that already knows the eventual current-build remedy to match from the opening state, while explicitly recording the diagnostic evidence it skips.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: a native-Wayland scaling interaction exposed by the Hyprland change affected WezTerm's known fractional-scaling path, causing the terminal surface to use only part of the window.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the non-default monitor scale reproductions, resize behavior or trace, and raw Hyprland bisection result rather than inferred from the screenshot alone.
Must recommend testing a current WezTerm nightly/git build containing the merged scaling fix while keeping native Wayland enabled; disabling Wayland is only a workaround, not the final fix.
Must not present adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size=false as the solution because the reporter tried it and the quarter-sized content remained.
If a manual doubled or quadrupled DPI workaround is present, it should be removed and WezTerm fully terminated and restarted before evaluating the fixed build.

Must ask the affected user to verify that the terminal fills the window on a build containing the fix before declaring reporter-verified resolution; the thread only establishes that another affected user could no longer reproduce it, while the original reporter could not retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Linux desktop user comfortable editing Lua configuration, using AUR/git packages, changing Hyprland window rules, collecting environment-variable logs, and testing compositor behavior, but not experienced with repository bisection or WezTerm internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, appreciative, and cooperative; gives detailed answers and configuration snippets, apologizes for delays, and distinguishes effective workarounds from the preferred native-Wayland outcome. Additional affected users contribute concise technical reproduction and bisection evidence.
